scope_allowed: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

models.name: HH-Explicit
models.what_it_computes: Coupled helmet–head explicit finite element analysis of skull stress fields and whole-head linear and angular kinematics with helmet structural and contact response

models.name: BH-Explicit
models.what_it_computes: Bare-head explicit finite element analysis resolving skull strain and brain deformation metrics (e.g., peak principal strain proxies and relative brain–skull motion) without helmet influence

mechanisms.name: Linear drop to rigid anvil
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Dominated by translational deceleration and normal contact, it governs skull stress and peak linear head acceleration relevant to skull fracture and focal injury thresholds

mechanisms.name: Oblique impact with tangential load
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Produces coupled normal–tangential loading and head rotation, governing angular kinematics and brain shear deformation associated with diffuse injury risk

deviation.detail: Credibility scores reported on a 0–5 scale per factor and per (model × mechanism) pair, where higher values denote stronger evidence

expected_decision.outcome_source: The practical consequence for decision-makers is that the simulation program can be used confidently to identify worst-case impact locations and speeds for linear drops and to evaluate how variations in liner and slip parameters influence both head kinematics and skull stress.

datasets: neutral-density target (NDT) clusters tracked by biplanar high-speed radiography
acceptance_criteria: proxies for peak principal strain within brain tissue

expected_context_of_use: In practice, the models are used to predict skull stress and brain-relevant kinematics across standardized linear and oblique impacts and to demonstrate performance against predefined acceptance thresholds.

spans: For HH-Explicit under linear drop, the refinement pro-cess produced small changes in the two most decision-relevant outputs: the grid convergence index (GCI) was 3.6% for peak resultant head acceleration and 4.2% for peak skull von Mises stress.
findings.span: For HH-Explicit under linear drop, the refinement pro-cess produced small changes in the two most decision-relevant outputs: the grid convergence index (GCI) was 3.6% for peak resultant head acceleration and 4.2% for peak skull von Mises stress.

spans: For HH-Explicit under oblique loading, the role of tangential contact and running slip increased the sensitivity to local mesh resolution at the slip interface and near shell curvature discontinuities; the GCI rose to 6.9% for peak angular velocity and 7.8% for peak angular acceleration.
findings.span: For HH-Explicit under oblique loading, the role of tangential contact and running slip increased the sensitivity to local mesh resolution at the slip interface and near shell curvature discontinuities; the GCI rose to 6.9% for peak angular velocity and 7.8% for peak angular acceleration.

spans: In linear drops the GCI was 3.9% for skull principal strain and 4.7% for the P95 of brain principal strain, while in oblique impacts it rose to 7.9% for brain–skull relative displacement and 8.4% for P95 principal strain.

spans: Analytic wave and patch tests showed <0.5% error; linear-momentum checked within 0.1% through a 6.0 m/s nor-mal impact.

spans: Sliding block and oblique con-tact benchmarks reproduced reference solutions within 0.8% error; total energy varia-tion <0.4% over 20 ms.

spans: HH-Explicit comprises a helmet shell and liner assembled over a human head model rooted in modern cranial anatomy.
findings.span: HH-Explicit comprises a helmet shell and liner assembled over a human head model rooted in modern cranial anatomy.

spans: The skull is modeled using a layered cortical–trabecular rep-resentation with regionally varying thickness (1.8–7.0 mm), each layer assigned orthotropic elastic–plastic properties tuned against bending and in-plane tests, and joined by cohesive interfaces that represent diploe transitions.
findings.span: The skull is modeled using a layered cortical–trabecular rep-resentation with regionally varying thickness (1.8–7.0 mm), each layer assigned orthotropic elastic–plastic properties tuned against bending and in-plane tests, and joined by cohesive interfaces that represent diploe transitions.

spans: BH-Explicit isolates the bare head to focus on skull and brain mechanics.
findings.span: BH-Explicit isolates the bare head to focus on skull and brain mechanics.

spans: The brain is represented by a nearly incompressible visco-hyperelastic law with shear relaxation times spanning 0.1–100 ms and a low-frequency storage modulus of 0.6–0.8 kPa, consistent with rheometry and inverse identification from kinematics.
